forecasts.question: Will at least 50 commercial vessels per day transit the Strait of Hormuz (50%+ of pre-war ~120/day baseline) during any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.38 → 0.33. IMF PortWatch May 26 data place Hormuz commercial transits at approximately 2% of pre-war baseline — roughly 2-3 vessels against a pre-war ~95/day figure. Maersk, MSC, Frontline, and BP tankers remain suspended. Lloyd's war-risk premium stands at ~5% of hull versus the 1.5% threshold at which Western insurers have historically resumed scheduled service. The US Navy Operation Project Freedom escort program has not resumed at scale. No signed MOU exists between the US and Iran; Trump's 'largely negotiated' language (NPR, May 23) has not been confirmed by a document. The PGSA third-party toll regime (announced May 18 per Axios) has not received commercial-entity confirmation from Lloyd's, Windward, or UNCTAD. A 25x increase in daily transits within 14 remaining days is not achievable absent a signed deal closing before approximately June 3. Judge: Analyst at 0.30 (too low given genuine deal momentum); DA at 0.45 (too high given insurance constraint is binding independent of verbal signals). Settled at 0.33, reflecting real but structurally blocked progress.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor (or UNCTAD, or Lloyd's List) reports ≥50 daily transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Lloyd's List Intelligence (primary, elevated from secondary per hygiene fix 2026-05-27), Windward (co-primary), Hormuz Strait Monitor (secondary — no institutional backing named for primary tier), UNCTAD Maritime Trade quarterly report (lagging confirmation).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If only Iranian-flagged or sanctions-evading dark-fleet vessels make up the count, but Western insurers still refuse: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (the operationally meaningful question is whether Western shipping has returned). PGSA addendum (Judge, 2026-05-19, reaffirmed 2026-05-27): third-country vessels (Chinese, Indian, Turkish) transiting under Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority toll regime count ONLY IF ≥2 of Lloyd's List/Windward/UNCTAD/Hormuz Strait Monitor confirm them as independent commercial entities not under IRGC-linked tolls (defined per US/EU/UK IRGC designation lists); PGSA self-reported numbers are excluded from resolution sourcing.

indicators.name: Lloyd's war-risk premium reduced below 1.5% of hull
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; insurance is the binding constraint on commercial transit regardless of verbal diplomatic progress.

indicators.name: Maersk/MSC/Frontline announce return to scheduled Hormuz transit
indicators.expected_effect: +25pp toward YES; major shipping lines lead the resumption and will not move without insurance clearance.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's governing coalition lose its 61-seat Knesset majority (via defection, dissolution motion, or no-confidence) before the mandatory 2026-10-27 election date?
forecasts.delta_reason: No probability update — weekly cadence (Wednesday). Material development logged: Knesset dissolution bill passed preliminary reading 110-0 on May 20 (Times of Israel, JPost, Haaretz). This is a coalition-submitted dissolution bill, not a Degel HaTorah opposition no-confidence motion — indicator design distinction preserved. The bill requires committee deliberation and two further plenary readings before final passage; no final vote has occurred. DA assessment: p=0.35 is understated (DA suggests 0.55-0.60 given formal dissolution process underway). Judge: Wednesday cadence rule is a hard constraint; intra-week update not permitted per Codex DA #12. Preliminary reading is a material procedural advance. Full reassessment required at Sunday May 31 cold-start audit. Anticipated cold-start revision: likely 0.50-0.60.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. The dissolution must complete all three Knesset readings and be formally signed. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel confirmation. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: counts as YES (majority lost). If a single party (e.g. Smotrich) departs but coalition retains 61+: counts as NO. Dissolution bill must pass final (third) Knesset reading to trigger YES via that mechanism. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas allowed per Codex DA #12.

indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; would also trigger Haredi reconsideration of remaining in government.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US confirm a signed written framework agreement (any named successor to the 14-point MOU) before EOD 2026-06-03?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.25 → 0.36. Trump publicly stated the deal was 'largely negotiated' (NPR, May 23). Rubio called it 'a pretty solid thing on the table' on Hormuz and 'a real significant time-limited negotiation on nuclear matters' (Al Jazeera, May 24). Iranian FM Araghchi, Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf, and Central Bank Governor Hemmati traveled to Doha May 25 to brief Qatar's leadership and examine frozen Iranian assets — a logistics-track preparation consistent with pre-implementation planning (Al Arabiya, The National). Three named independent sources across different outlets within 48 hours constitute a genuine evidence cluster. However: Araghchi stated May 27 he was unsure whether a deal was imminent (Reuters). Khamenei advisor Shamkhani dismissed US nuclear-control demands as 'fantasy' (Al Jazeera, May 27). Axios May 24 reporting identified a 12-15 year gap on enrichment duration and an unresolved Hormuz tolls dispute. No signed document exists. Horizon compressed from June 5 to June 3 per current intelligence on the Axios-reported June 3 target date; N2 (separate June 3 forecast) folded into this forecast rather than creating two overlapping Iran-US deal forecasts. Ambiguity rule updated: Witkoff signing with White House readout satisfies YES (hierarchy conflict resolved). Judge: Analyst at 0.34, DA at 0.38-0.42; settled at 0.36.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official AND a named Iranian official publicly confirm a signed written framework (by any name); OR if the document text is published by Axios/Reuters/State Dept or Iran MFA with both parties acknowledging authenticity. Verbal 'agreement in principle' does not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At minimum, Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP quoting named US AND Iranian principals (not envoys alone). Official Iranian Foreign Ministry statement or State Dept press release also resolves. Witkoff signing with concurrent White House press office readout = YES (envoy-plus-principal-confirmation hierarchy).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreement by envoys only, without principal confirmation (Trump/Pezeshkian) within 72h of announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran signs but Khamenei's office disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Witkoff signing WITH White House press office readout published within 24h = YES (satisfies US principal-confirmation requirement). 'Largely negotiated' or similar verbal statements without a document = NO.

indicators.name: Witkoff/Araghchi direct meeting confirmed (not via Pakistan or Qatar intermediary)
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; Araghchi and Ghalibaf present in Doha May 25 for preparatory logistics track — direct bilateral Witkoff meeting not yet confirmed.

indicators.name: Trump public statement calling deal 'beautiful' or 'done'
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; 'largely negotiated' language (May 23) is partial but not the threshold framing; 'beautiful' or 'done' is the historical pre-announcement pattern.

forecasts.question: Will the Lebanon 45-day ceasefire extension (announced May 15) formally collapse — defined as US withdrawal of sponsorship OR Lebanese government publicly declaring the truce void — before EOD 2026-05-22?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO at horizon. The US State Department did not withdraw sponsorship before EOD May 22 — instead it scheduled a security track reconvening at the Pentagon on May 29 and a political track on June 2-3, maintaining active institutional sponsorship (CNBC, PBS, GlobalSecurity). The Lebanese government did not declare the truce void. IDF strikes in southern Lebanon continued through May 22, including the killing of six paramedics; Hezbollah fired rockets in retaliation. Neither party nor the United States formally declared the ceasefire void. The resolution criteria required a formal US or Lebanese government withdrawal statement, which was not issued.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the US State Department or Lebanese Foreign Ministry issues a public statement explicitly declaring the ceasefire void or withdrawn; OR if IDF and Hezbollah resume sustained exchange at pre-April-16 intensity (>50 launches/day from each side) and both US and Lebanon acknowledge breakdown. Individual violations do NOT resolve YES.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept press release or named spokesperson; OR Lebanese government official quoted in Reuters/AP/AFP; OR combined IDF/LBAF situation reports showing pre-truce intensity levels.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: IDF strikes in south Lebanon outside Beirut governorate = NOT collapse (consistent with current porous-truce pattern). Hezbollah verbal threat to resume without acting = NOT collapse. Collapse requires formal withdrawal of US or Lebanese government support.

indicators.name: IDF airstrike on Beirut governorate within 72h of ceasefire extension
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; would demonstrate US tolerance for truce violation at capital level.

indicators.name: Hezbollah rocket barrage >50/day from south Litani
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; mass rocket fire historically triggers Israeli large-scale response and truce void.

forecasts.question: Will the US-Israel-Lebanon Pentagon security track meeting scheduled for May 29 produce a written outcome document (communiqué, framework, or joint statement) confirmed by officials from both the US and Lebanese sides by EOD 2026-05-30?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assignment. The US State Department and Pentagon publicly announced the security track for May 29 following the May 15 45-day ceasefire extension. Both US and Lebanese Armed Forces delegations have accepted the format per institutional communications (CNBC, PBS, GlobalSecurity). The residual risk is a last-minute delegation withdrawal triggered by ground escalation in southern Lebanon — IDF strikes continued through May 26 and Hezbollah retaliated with rockets — but the US's active sponsorship role historically maintains institutional formats even through active violations. Base rate for a scheduled Pentagon-hosted security track producing a written readout, given both delegations confirmed and US sponsorship active, is high. Resolution threshold is a written outcome document (not merely a verbal summary) confirmed by both sides.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US Defense Dept or CENTCOM official AND a named Lebanese Armed Forces or Israeli defense official jointly confirm a written outcome document (communiqué, framework, or joint statement) by EOD 2026-05-30. Verbal summaries only = NO.

forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Joint press conference without written document = NO. Outcome document acknowledged by only one side within 24h of EOD May 30 = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Meeting postponed but held before EOD May 30 = still eligible for YES if written document produced.

forecasts.question: Will the Lebanon 45-day ceasefire (extended May 15, running to approximately June 29) remain formally intact — with both US sponsorship and Lebanese government adherence maintained — through EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assignment. The Lebanon ceasefire did not formally collapse by its May 22 first test (F4 resolved NO). The US-sponsored security track reconvenes at the Pentagon May 29; political talks scheduled June 2-3. Both the US and Lebanon have maintained formal sponsorship through May 26. IDF strikes in southern Lebanon killed over 650 people since the ceasefire extension, including six paramedics on May 22 (Al Jazeera); Hezbollah fired rockets in response; Ben-Gvir called for 'large-scale combat' May 25 (Al Jazeera); Washington Post reported the ceasefire 'faltering' May 26. The question is whether the formal framework — defined as US sponsorship plus Lebanese government adherence — survives to June 10. The Pentagon track May 29 and political track June 2-3 create institutional lock-in. Formal collapse requires an explicit US State Dept or Lebanese FM declaration, which neither has made. The porous-truce pattern established since April 16 resolves YES under the ambiguity rule unless a government-level withdrawal statement is issued.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if both US sponsorship (no State Dept withdrawal statement) and Lebanese government formal adherence are maintained through EOD 2026-06-10. NO if the US State Department withdraws sponsorship OR the Lebanese FM or PM publicly declares the truce void before that date.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept named spokesperson or press release; Lebanese PM or FM statement quoted in Reuters/AP/AFP. Silence (no withdrawal statement from either party) resolves YES.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: IDF strikes in south Lebanon without US State Dept withdrawal = NOT collapse (ceasefire is acknowledged porous per established pattern). Hezbollah rocket fire without Lebanese FM declaration = NOT collapse. Only a formal US or Lebanese government withdrawal statement triggers NO resolution. Individual daily strikes below pre-truce intensity = YES (porous truce intact). Hezbollah verbal threat without action = YES.

indicators.name: Pentagon security track convenes as scheduled May 29 with both Israeli and Lebanese military delegations
indicators.expected_effect: +12pp toward YES; institutional engagement is an anti-collapse signal that reinforces US sponsorship commitment.

indicators.name: IDF airstrike on Beirut governorate or IDF publicly declares ceasefire void
indicators.expected_effect: -25pp toward YES; capital-level escalation or IDF declaration would trigger immediate US sponsorship withdrawal review.
